paraphrase: Deities who were disciples of rival teachers speak before the Buddha: one praises Pūraṇa, who saw no evil in injuring and killing nor merit for oneself; one praises Makkhali, well restrained by austerity and scruple, truthful, shunning quarrels; one praises the Nigaṇṭha, scrupulous, restrained by the fourfold restraint; one praises Pakudha and the others as not far from the good. Another deity answers that the jackal never equals the lion; Māra, possessing him, praises those devoted to austerity and heaven, and the Buddha exposes Māra's bait.
notes: Reported by an opponent: deities in a Buddhist text (SN 2.30, Buddhist Pali canon). Section refs = SuttaCentral (bilara) segmentation, checked in the local e-text. Only here does a Pali text give praise-verses for the rival teachers, in the mouths of their former disciples.
